business_scope.primary_industry_name: Legal Accounting Defense for International Anti-Dumping Inquiries

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Cairo as commercial and administrative capital; single national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-inspired codified tradition; Islamic Sharia is the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; commercial incorporation and trade-remedy matters adjudicated by Economic Courts)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Over 100 active bilateral investment treaties and more than 50 double taxation avoidance agreements, including DTAAs with the UK, France, Germany, UAE and China; Egypt is a WTO member bound by the ADA Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014, Law No. 44 of 2015 and Law No. 154 of 2019; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003; Ministry of Investment Decree No. 44 of 2020 establishing the Beneficial Owner Register, as amended by Ministerial Decree No. 133 of 2021; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry or equivalent corporate registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via Egyptian Embassy or Consulate (Egypt is not a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certified registry extract for the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry or trade register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of board or shareholder resolution authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing its general manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of origin followed by Consular Legalization via Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport and national ID copies of each ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Consular Legalization via Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter signature verified by home-country notary and Consular Legalization via Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, general managers and authorized signatories against the EMLCU national terrorist financing list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions, MENAFATF regional advisories and the Egyptian Ministry of Interior watchlist; enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth documentation required for any politically exposed person per Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended; continuous re-screening triggers on name changes, share transfers above 25%, or ministerial sanctions updates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Investor Services Electronic Platform at gafi.gov.eg and the Commercial Registry automated system implementing Law No. 34 of 1976
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in Arabic script and must end with the Arabic legal form suffix شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة (LLC); a Latin-alphabet transliteration may be shown as an additional trade name provided it phonetically matches the Arabic name; the Arabic name must be identical and internally consistent across the Articles of Association, the commercial registry card (sijil), tax card and official letterhead; names implying political, military, religious or misleading commercial connotations are forbidden.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: مصر / Egyptian (Misr or Egypt) – restricted one-word use requiring special approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the GAFI Grievance Committee within 15 business days from the notice of refusal, submitting up to three alternative names and a consent letter from the conflicting-name registrant where applicable; if the objection is denied, a judicial appeal may be brought before the Economic Court within 60 days under Articles 5 and 7 of Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; a name reservation can be extended once for an additional 30 days by paying the renewal fee before the original window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a purely remote or virtual mailing address. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical registered office in Egypt where the corporate seal, statutory books, social insurance file and tax records are maintained; serviced shared office space with a dedicated workstation, local administrative staff and nameplate is acceptable for an ISIC 7490 trade-defense consultancy, but a PO Box or teleworking-only address will trigger registration refusal and subsequent administrative sanctions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Initial premises verification at formation is mandatory and effectively 100%; post-incorporation, unannounced on-site inspection risk for a low-risk professional services LLC is approximately 15-20% annually and increases if the registered address is a shared multi-tenant serviced office or is changed more than once in a calendar year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee per Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 service schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Articles 102–143 (Limited Liability Companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies and Commercial Registry Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation application using the standardized GAFI form together with notarized Articles of Association (Company Contract).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Egyptian law imposes no fixed minimum paid-up capital for an LLC providing professional services, provided that the subscribed capital is fully declared in the Articles of Association and that at least 50% of the declared subscribed capital is deposited in a bank account opened in the company's name at an Egyptian bank before registration. The deposit is treated as escrowed capital and may be withdrawn only after receipt of the final incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the shareholders' subscription to the issued quotas totalling EGP 50,000, deposited with National Bank of Egypt under reference CN-21-0902, be approved; (2) that the registered office be fixed at [Registered Address, Cairo Governorate] for all statutory notices; (3) that [Director Name] and [Director Name] be appointed Directors of the Company, and [Corporate Secretary Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary; (4) that the Corporate Secretary is deputized to execute all GAFI incorporation forms and bank account documentation; and (5) that the notarized Articles of Association be filed with GAFI and the tax registry tax card be obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Companies Registration Directorate (online Commercial Names System).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the preferred company name (Arabic transliteration) and up to two fallback names through the GAFI online portal. The system checks for conflicts with existing trademarks and registered company names. Upon clearance, GAFI issues a name approval certificate valid for 60 days. The name must include 'LLC' or equivalent Arabic expression.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name reservation application
Clearance search request
Copy of each shareholder's national ID or passport
Power of attorney if a local agent is engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, file a rehearing petition with GAFI's Grievance Committee within 15 days, or resubmit with a distinctive suffix and a risk-aversion memorandum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Founding Statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Office of the Egyptian Land Registry and Notarization Authority (Shahr Al-Aqari).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Association before a licensed notary public. All shareholders or their legal representatives must sign in person, confirming the allocation of quotas, registered office address, corporate purpose (ISIC 7490) and the first directors. The notary then stamps and records the notarized instrument in the Register of Companies' underlying contracts.
required_dossiers: Drafted Articles of Association (Arabic or bilingual)
Shareholders' proof of identity and copies of passports/NIDs
Tax identification numbers of all shareholders (if any)
Detailed corporate purpose statement referencing anti-dumping trade defense services
Notarial stamp fee receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a defect, rectify the instrument by a lawfully approved addendum and re-notarize the revised pages; the original notarial certificate must be canceled or amended before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Opening at a Licensed Egyptian Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate bank account in the company's name. Deposit at least 50% of the subscribed capital (EGP 25,000 out of EGP 50,000). Obtain a capital escrow certificate from the bank certifying the deposit, the account number, and the legal capacity of the depositor. The bank will release the funds only after the GAFI incorporation certificate is presented.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
Name approval certificate from GAFI
Valid ID or passport of the authorized signatory
Board resolution authorizing the bank account opening (pre-registration resolution)
Bank account application forms and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank challenges the incomplete pre-registration documents, obtain a GAFI provisional certificate of intention to incorporate or have the authorized counsel execute a legal opinion in support of the account opening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with GAFI and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Investment Window / One-Shop Service Center (Cairo headquarters or online portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file to GAFI, either electronically through the GAFI digital platform or physically at the One-Shop Service Center. Attach the notarized Articles, name approval, capital escrow certificate, and identity documents. Pay the statutory incorporation fees, which include registration, publication, and stamp duties. GAFI then issues a formal receipt and commences the statutory review.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
GAFI name clearance certificate
Bank escrow capital certificate
Clearance of security background checks for ultimate beneficial owners
GAFI fee payment voucher
Board resolution appointing the legal representative and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or request for amendment, respond within 30 days with corrected documents; if the application is refused, submit a legal appeal to the GAFI Ministerial Appeals Commission or the Economic Administrative Court within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Incorporation Certificate, Tax Card and Commercial Registry Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI in coordination with the Egyptian Tax Authority and the Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Justice).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the statutory review, GAFI issues the company's incorporation certificate. This certificate is automatically transmitted to the Commercial Registry for entry into the national commercial register, and to the Egyptian Tax Authority for the issuance of the tax card and VAT registration certificate. After these procedures the company is legally constituted and may begin operations after licensing.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation decision or certificate
Bank escrow release form
Commercial registry entry payment receipt
Tax card application and official VAT forms
Certificate of the directors' no-objection letters from security authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry refuses entry due to a mismatch or missing endorsement, obtain a GAFI correction certificate and file a registry rectification petition; the tax card may be reissued by the local tax authority if delayed beyond the standard SLA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – International Trade Policies and Negotiations Sector, together with GAFI's Investor Services Center (for professional services operating license).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration Certificate (Hijria) for Professional Services and Trade Remedy Defense Consulting (ISIC 7490).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Environmental Licensing Directorate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (C) – Registration Only / Exempt from Full EIA Report, as the activity is exclusively office-based professional consulting with no manufacturing, pilot plant, or hazardous material handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and Decree No. 944 of 2007 on ambient air quality is confined to indoor office ventilation and standby generator emission thresholds. Wastewater shall be discharged exclusively into municipal sewers below Egyptian sewer standards (allowed BOD ≤ 600 mg/L). No VOC emission sources are installed; paper and electronic waste shall be managed under EEAA waste tracking instructions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain a Fire Safety and Civil Defense Certificate from the General Directorate of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) confirming acceptable building fire load, emergency exits, smoke detection, and fire-extinguishing systems. In addition, a Occupational Safety and Health Clearance from the Ministry of Manpower and a Structural Compatibility Certificate from the District/City Municipality are required, verifying that the office premises meet seismic load and operational density requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory VAT registration (Art. 24, Law 67/2016); simplified small-supplier registration is available for turnover below the threshold

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (شهادة تحويل للداخل) evidencing foreign-currency receipt

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE; Al-Bank Al-Markazi Al-Masri), the exclusive foreign-exchange and monetary authority of the Arab Republic of Egypt, operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 promulgating the Central Bank and Banking System Law (which repealed the former Law No. 88 of 2003) and the anti-money laundering framework of Law No. 80 of 2002 as subsequently amended; the CBE discharges FX oversight through its authorized dealer bank network, the unified-float decisions of 6 March 2024, and its commitments under the IMF Extended Fund Facility; all cross-border remittances affecting Egyptian residents require CBE e-form registration and bank intermediation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP operates under a CBE-managed flexible exchange-rate regime in which current-account transactions (trade in goods and services) are fully convertible for resident commercial entities through licensed onshore banks, subject to the CBE electronic e-form platform, documentary proof (notarized service contracts, commercial invoices, tax registrations, and, where relevant, ACI/NAFEZA import registrations), and bank-level customer due diligence. Capital-account transactions are likewise permitted: inbound equity contributions, foreign loans, and capital repatriation require GAFI investment registration and CBE purpose-code classification, while outbound profit remittance (dividends) requires audited financial statements, board dividend minutes, an Egyptian Tax Authority clearance certificate, and a CBE e-form declaration. The practical hurdles are documentary and administrative rather than legal: incomplete underlying files halt conversion, and during periods of acute liquidity stress the spread between onshore interbank and offshore quotations may widen, producing an economic rather than statutory convertibility constraint; profit-remittance restrictions are not currently in force for a tax-compliant LLC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The current statutory regime applies a 0% mandatory conversion ratio: the CBE has abolished compulsory surrender of export and service-export proceeds, and the Egyptian LLC may lawfully retain 100% of its foreign-currency service receivables in onshore Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs) at authorized dealer banks. The residual mandatory obligation is repatriation: all export and service proceeds must be credited through an Egyptian-licensed authorized dealer bank within the CBE-monitored repatriation deadlines (the bank-applied benchmark for services is the contractual payment maturity, with the CBE inspection reference ceiling for goods being five months from shipment/transport documentation and banks applying a parallel discipline to substantial service receivables); collection through unlicensed offshore channels does not discharge the repatriation duty, and non-compliant exporters are recorded in the CBE exporter-compliance registry, risking restriction of future bank operations and AML/CFT review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EGP Account plus USD/EUR Foreign Currency Account; dedicated inward-FDI registration sub-account segregating capital proceeds pending GAFI-CBE registration
Operational EGP Account plus USD Foreign Currency Account with ancillary trade-services overlay supporting SWIFT MT103 service disbursements and e-forms
Operational EGP Account plus multi-currency Foreign Currency Account; preferred digital treasury desk for e-form initiation, online FX execution, and same-day corporate banking
Operational EGP Account plus Global USD/EUR Foreign Currency Account supporting international payroll, cross-border cash pooling, and multi-region clearing for trade-remedy defense engagements
Operational EGP Account plus USD Foreign Currency Account as contingency diversification of banking counterparty risk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. No offshore electronic money institution (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, or comparable) holds a CBE banking license issuable under Law No. 194 of 2020; CBE repatriation rules require corporate service-export receivables to be collected through an Egyptian-licensed authorized dealer bank. EMIs may therefore serve only as auxiliary low-value disbursement cards for incidental travel and data expenses and never as the primary inbound receivable rail; reliance on unlicensed EMIs for the collection of the LLC's professional fees would constitute a CBE repatriation breach and attract adverse AML/CFT findings by Egyptian compliance authorities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory face-to-face presence is required for at least one authorized signatory at corporate account opening under CBE AML Law No. 80 of 2002, its Executive Regulation (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 626 of 2015, as amended), and standard authorized-dealer account-acceptance policies; fully remote corporate onboarding is not available for non-resident directors. Non-resident directors may execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney appointing an Egyptian-resident authorized signatory for day-to-day transactions, but the ultimate account principal (the authorized deal signatory) must still attend the initial KYC interview in person at the branch; subsequent operations may be conducted through issued corporate internet-banking tokens and signed SWIFT-file instructions, and the bank retains the right to request periodic in-person re-verification under ongoing due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The corporate scope (legal accounting defense for international anti-dumping inquiries with substantial cross-border professional-service receivables) is ineligible for simplified due diligence and may be screened as a trade-based money laundering or sanctions-evasion pattern given the involvement of steel, aluminum, ceramics, tires, and chemical exporters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (i) GAFI investment license and Commercial Registry extract; (ii) Egyptian tax card and VAT certificate; (iii) executed engagement letters identifying each WTO, EU, US (DOC/USITC), Turkey, GCC, or South Africa trade-remedy proceeding by docket number; (iv) complete UBO register identifying all natural persons holding 25% or more, with passport copies, source-of-wealth statements, and bank references; (v) audited financial statements; (vi) professional indemnity insurance certificate evidencing genuine operational substance; (vii) itemized client fee schedule and service-level agreement; (viii) where legal opinions are rendered, joint engagement with members of the Egyptian Bar licensed under Law No. 17 of 1983 to avoid unlawful practice-of-law classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment pattern: the contractual importer of record, the legal beneficiary of the defense services, and the remitting treasury entity are different legal persons (e.g., a foreign group treasury center forwards funds on behalf of an exporter-client).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (i) executed third-party payment authorization letters for each receivable; (ii) group organization chart establishing the treasury center mandate; (iii) intra-group cost-allocation and intercompany agreements; (iv) SWIFT MT103 advices identifying the true remitter; (v) invoice-by-invoice reconciliation statement linking the trade-remedy defense work to the funded amount; (vi) signed timesheets and case-activity reports from the defense team demonstrating that services were actually rendered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the GAFI renewal window from 1 January to 31 March (calendar-year certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fine of EGP 500-2,000; delinquency beyond 90 days triggers suspension and administrative strike-off (deregistration) by GAFI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 33)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Corporate Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April following the 31 December standard fiscal year-end (within 4 months after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EGP 20,000 plus monthly delay interest of 2% of unpaid tax; chronic non-filing may trigger forced assessment, bank seizures, and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly Payroll (Salary Tax) Withholding Returns and Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Payroll Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly by the 15th of the following month; annual consolidated salary listing attached to the CIT return by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay interest of 2% plus fine of EGP 500-5,000 per unfiled or late monthly return; disallowance of deducted salaries as corporate tax deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Withholding Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly by the 15th of the following month for each withholding event; consolidated annual WHT return by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay interest of 2% plus administrative fines up to EGP 5,000; non-recovery of WHT from counterparties shifts liability to the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Shareholding Structure Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI - Beneficial Ownership Unit (AML Law No. 80 of 2002 register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing and any share-transfer update within 30 days; annual re-confirmation submitted with the commercial registry renewal by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EGP 100,000 under the AML framework and suspension of commercial registration until the UBO record is cured.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transfer Pricing Disclosure and Local File Availability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Transfer Pricing Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: TP disclosure attached to the annual CIT return by 30 April; complete local and master file to be furnished within 30 days of an ETA request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to EGP 100,000 under Decree No. 492 of 2019, automatic transfer pricing audit, shifted evidentiary burden, and secondary adjustment risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Professional Activity License Renewal - Anti-Dumping Trade Defense Consultancy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry (MOTI) - Trade Remedies Sector, coordinated with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Aligned with the annual commercial registry renewal by 31 March or the license anniversary date, whichever is earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License expiry voids trade-remedy representation acts and may subject the entity to fines for unlicensed practice; continued non-renewal leads to license revocation and deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors (ESAA)-licensed statutory auditor where LLC paid-up capital exceeds EGP 250,000; audit also required when GAFI, the ETA, or the professional license condition expressly demands audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), IFRS-consistent, as issued and updated by the Ministry of Finance and the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors (ESAA); IFRS is accepted for consolidated group and listed-entity reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Executive Regulations of AML Law No. 80 of 2002, the LLC must maintain with GAFI a full ownership chain, precise shareholding percentages, and the natural-person UBO of each quota-holder. Every share transfer must be formalized in a notarized deed, approved by the remaining partners under the LLC articles of association, and filed with the updated Register of Members within 30 days. The 31 March renewal submission re-confirms the UBO statement upon the managing director's declaration of accuracy.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Managers) and their shareholdings
Minute Book of General Assemblies and Manager Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,000-2,500 per year for a small professional-services LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% per Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 48, as amended by tax reforms effective January 2020.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic CIT holiday for an ISIC 7490 LLC. Investment Law No. 72/2017 projects may derive a refundable tax credit based on paid-up capital; entities licensed in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) may access special investment deductions and customs relief, subject to Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) approval. A final 10% profit-distribution tax applies when after-tax profits are distributed, which adds an effective 2.25 percentage points on a fully distributed profit stream.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 41 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed by all legal persons; mandatory electronic submission via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (portal.eta.gov.eg or the income tax e-service platform). A separate Transfer Pricing disclosure annex must be submitted with the return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (single 12-month period; calendar year or ETA-approved fiscal year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., April 30 for calendar-year taxpayers; October 31 for June 30 fiscal-year taxpayers). Residual CIT is payable at filing; statutory advance tax installments are credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ETA-assigned corporate tax file number and commercial-register number of the LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch must register with the ETA and use its local branch Tax Card; a foreign entity without an Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) does not file Form 41.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the tax year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE's approved fiscal year; a treaty-protected foreign entity must state the period in which the Egyptian-sourced income arose for WHT treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total billing including retainer fees, success fees, and reimbursed expenses from anti-dumping trade-defense consulting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Egypt-source revenue attributable to the PE; treaty-exempt income must be separately disclosed with a TRC reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of service delivery, subcontracted legal-economics expertise, and expert witness fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subcontractor payments to non-resident affiliates must satisfy the arm's length standard and TP documentation requirements.
Provide a profit-margin reconciliation if the PE is examined under a TP pricing method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains, and incidental non-operating receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest sourced from Egypt paid to a non-resident is separately subject to 20% WHT unless treaty relief is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries (with payroll-tax reconciliation), rent, utilities, software, bank charges, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-charges from foreign headquarters are deductible only with a TP Local File and evidence of actual benefit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation on fixed assets computed per ETA-prescribed useful lives and basis rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assets of a foreign branch are depreciated separately; treaty provisions do not alter the ETA depreciation regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Only deductible provisions (e.g., doubtful debts, employee end-of-service) per Articles 25 to 27 of Law 91/2005.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Contingency reserves with no current legal obligation are disallowed; non-resident PEs should avoid booking home-office discretionary reserves.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for tax additions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure PE results are booked against the ETA tax file; global group results are irrelevant to the PE-only computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses, limited to five years from the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change in 50% or more of ownership or a change of activity may trigger an ETA audit and loss-deduction denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after loss offset and any TP adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE, applies to Egypt-source profits; head-office overhead allocations must be TP-documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 22.5%; specific industries may face special rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branches are taxed at the same 22.5% rate; no reduced branch rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 14 - Tax Credits and Advance Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory advance installments, income tax withheld at source, and any refundable investment tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not available unless an applicable DTA expressly allows credit for taxes paid in the foreign contracting state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance payable to the ETA or refundable to the taxpayer after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Over-withholding on non-resident transactions should be claimed via a separate refund application with the ETA International Agreements Department.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of the value and methodology of all related-party transactions during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to file the annex triggers an automatic EGP 20,000 fine and loss of audit-marketing protection; non-resident counterparty data (tax residency, transaction value, method) must be complete.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed fine of EGP 3,000 to EGP 30,000. Unpaid tax: monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the tax due, capped at 20% of the principal tax. Failure to produce statutory books on audit request: EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000. Deliberate misreporting triggers criminal sanctions under Article 133 and potential imprisonment.
